{{Short description|Astronomical statement}}
The '''Freeman law''' is a statement in astronomy which says that [[disk galaxy|disk galaxies]] have the same [[surface brightness]], Σ at the center. It was described in 1970 by [[Ken Freeman (astronomer)|Ken Freeman]].<ref name="McGaugh">{{Cite journal|arxiv=astro-ph/9505062|last1=McGaugh|first1=S. S|title=Galaxy Selection and the Surface Brightness Distribution|journal=The Astronomical Journal|volume=110|issue=1995|pages=573|last2=Bothun|first2=G. D|last3=Schombert|first3=J. M|year=1995|doi=10.1086/117543|bibcode=1995AJ....110..573M|s2cid=119527623}}</ref><ref>{{cite journal|author=Freeman, Kenneth C.|title=On the disks of spiral and S0 galaxies|journal=The Astrophysical Journal|volume=160|issue=3|year=1970|pages=811–830|bibcode=1970ApJ...160..811F|doi=10.1086/150474|doi-access=free}}</ref>

More recently it has been argued that the Freeman law is an effect of [[selection bias]].<ref name="McGaugh" /><ref>Minnesota State University, "{{cite web |url=http://odin.physastro.mnsu.edu/~eskridge/astr225/week10.html |title=Archived copy |accessdate=2008-01-11 |url-status=dead |archiveurl=https://web.archive.org/web/20070706235131/http://odin.physastro.mnsu.edu/~eskridge/astr225/week10.html |archivedate=2007-07-06 }}"</ref> However, after accounting for selection effects, the Freeman law was confirmed in the year 2010 for a sample of 30000 [[Sloan Digital Sky Survey]] galaxy images.<ref name="Fathi">{{Cite journal|arxiv=1009.2692|last1=Fathi|first1=Kambiz|title=Revisiting the Scale Length-mu0 Plane and the Freeman Law in the Local Universe|journal=The Astrophysical Journal|volume=722|pages=L120–L125|year=2010|issue=1|doi=10.1088/2041-8205/722/1/L120|bibcode=2010ApJ...722L.120F|s2cid=119208149}}</ref> It can be used with the [[Tully–Fisher relation]] to determine the [[luminosity]] and therefore distance of an observed galaxy.

The Freeman law is sometimes called the Fish-Freeman effect.<ref>{{cite journal|author=Disney, M.|author2=Phillipps, S.|year=1983|title=The visibility of galaxies as a function of central surface brightness|journal=Monthly Notices of the Royal Astronomical Society|volume=205|issue=4|pages=1253–1265|doi=10.1093/mnras/205.4.1253|bibcode=1983MNRAS.205.1253D|doi-access=free}}</ref>

==Fish law==
The '''Fish law''' (or Fish's law) in astronomy is the analogue for the Freeman law with disk galaxies replaced by [[Elliptical galaxy|elliptical galaxies]]. It was described in 1964 by Robert A. Fish based on photometric results for 29 elliptical galaxies.<ref>{{cite journal|author=Fish, Robert A.|title=A Mass-Potential Relationship in Elliptical Galaxies and Some Inferences Concerning the Formation and Evolution of Galaxies|journal=The Astrophysical Journal|volume=139|issue=1|year=1964|pages=284–305|bibcode=1964ApJ...139..284F|doi=10.1086/147753|doi-access=free}}</ref>

==Modified Newtonian Dynamics (MOND)==
According to Brada and [[Mordehai Milgrom|Milgrom]],<ref>{{Cite journal|author=Brada, Rafael|author2=Milgrom, Mordehai|title=The modified dynamics (MOND) predicts an absolute maximum to the acceleration produced by 'dark halos'|journal=The Astrophysical Journal|volume=512|issue=17|pages=L17|date=December 1998|arxiv=astro-ph/9812117|doi=10.1086/311871|bibcode=1999ApJ...512L..17B|s2cid=117804800}}</ref>
{{blockquote|The acceleration constant of the modified dynamics ([[MOND]]), ''a<sub>0</sub>'', appears in various predicted regularities pertinent to galaxies. For example, it features as an upper cutoff to the mean surface density (or mean surface brightness translated with ''[[List of common astronomy symbols#Mass comparison|M]]/[[List of common astronomy symbols#Luminosity comparison|L]]'') of galaxies, as observed and formulated in the Freeman law for disks, and of the Fish law for ellipticals.}}
